The Chinese invasion of Vietnam in 1979, a part of the Sino-Vietnamese War, was a short but intense conflict that lasted from February 17 to March 16, 1979. China launched the invasion in response to Vietnam's invasion and occupation of Cambodia in 1978, which overthrew the China-backed Khmer Rouge regime. China aimed to "teach Vietnam a lesson" for its growing ties with the Soviet Union, China's rival.
Chinese forces crossed the northern border of Vietnam, attacking several provinces. They faced stiff resistance from Vietnamese troops and militias, many of whom were experienced from the Vietnam War. After about a month of fighting, China declared its objectives met and withdrew, though it did not achieve a decisive victory. Both sides claimed success, but the war left tens of thousands dead and damaged relations for years.
